newsitem.title: INDIA: New tea brand sales touch 1.0 bln rupees in 96-HLL.
newsitem.headline: New tea brand sales touch 1.0 bln rupees in 96-HLL.

text.p: India's Hindustan Lever (HLL) on Friday said its Brooke Bond A1 brand of tea, launched in 1996, had notched up one billion rupees in sales.
Priced at a marginal premium to loose tea, the launch of Brooke Bond A1 was one of the biggest developments in the Indian tea market in 1996, the company said in a statement.
The brand was aimed at converting users of loose (unpackaged, unbranded) tea, which accounts for two-thirds of the Indian market, to the more hygienic packet tea segment.
The company, which has merged with another Unilever firm Brooke Bond Lipton India Ltd, which was handling tea, said the tea business registered excellent growth in 1996.
HLL said it was the world's largest branded tea business.
"In India, one out of every two cups of branded tea consumed is from the company's portfolio," a company statement said.

"An indication of the business strength is that seven brands of the company -- Brooke Bond Red Label, Brooke Bond Taj Mahal, Lipton Taaza, Brooke Bond A1, Brooke Bond 3 Roses, Brooke Bond Super Dust and Lipton Top Star -- are among India's top 10 packet tea brands."

Other existing brands consolidated their positions during the year. Simultaneously, an integrated bush-to-brand supply chain management helped improve profitability through reducition of working capital by over 25 percent during the year, it said.
Manufacturing facilities have been mobilised in close proximity to major consumption areas to provide fresher tea, Hindustan Lever said.
The firm's plantations performed well during the year.
"The per yield per hectare of Doom Dooma and Tea Estates is among the best in the industry," it said.
